subject: Post-call recap: token profile, unit economics & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Chen <anna@fastpay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: token profile, unit economics & next steps

Anna — thanks again for a productive call today. Below is a concise recap and a few asks so we can move the pricing conversation to procurement. Please confirm or correct any numbers.

Call highlights (rough):
- Primary use case: multi-turn customer support + personalized recommendations in web & mobile chat.
- Expected active users: 35k monthly active; peak concurrent sessions ~250.
- Typical session structure: 1–3 prompt turns from user, 1 model completion. We expect API calls per session to be roughly 1.6 on average.

Token profile (from the sample logs you shared; attached CSV):
- Average prompt tokens per API call: 420 tokens (median 290).
- Average completion tokens per API call: 180 tokens (median 120).
- Estimated total tokens per API call (prompt + completion): 600 tokens on average.
- Distribution: ~72% of calls fit within 8k context, ~24% require 32k to keep history for multi-turns, ~4% are long-form cases that would benefit from 128k context (batch uploads / billing disputes).

Monthly volume scenarios (rounded):
- Conservative (pilot): 2M API calls -> ~1.2B total tokens / month.
- Mid (Q4 scale): 12M API calls -> ~7.2B total tokens / month.
- Peak (full roll-out): 30M API calls -> ~18B total tokens / month.

Pricing / unit economics notes for discussion:
- Target unit economics you mentioned: target ~$70–$120 / 1M tokens (you said you needed target cost to align with current ML spend).
- For Redwood internal modeling: at 7.2B tokens/mo, a $100 / 1M tokens rate equals $720k / month.

Asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm which volume scenario looks closest to your procurement budget (Conservative / Mid / Peak) and the target monthly spend range.
2) Confirm the % of calls needing 32k vs 128k context (we used the sample as above — if you have a labeled breakdown by feature we can refine).
3) If procurement wants a pilot, what length and budget would you prefer (we typically do 30–60 day pilots with token caps and usage monitoring)?
4) Do you have any hard constraints (SLA, data retention, KMS) that we should include in the procurement doc?

Attachments: FastPay_token_sample_summary.csv (CSV with sampled call-level token counts), redwood-pricing-estimate-v1.pdf (high-level unit econ scenarios).

Proposed immediate next step: procurement intro + pilot SOW draft if you confirm pilot interest. I can send an initial SOW and a simple pricing table once you confirm the target scenario.

Thanks — I’ll hold on pricing until you confirm volume and pilot preference.

—
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Anna Chen <anna@fastpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token profile, unit economics & next steps

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap and for attaching the sample. The numbers look close to what we see; a couple of clarifications below:

1) Volume stance: Mid is our planning target for Q4 (we expect to cross 10–14M calls/month if the pilot goes well). We don’t expect Peak yet — that’s a FY27 goal.
2) Context breakdown: your split is accurate for feature X (support chat). For feature Y (billing/appeals) the long context usage is slightly higher — call that 8% needing 128k.
3) Budget: procurement has given us a mid-tier target of $600k–$850k/month for the model spend line item (not counting infra or ops).

Pilot ask: let’s do a 45-day pilot capped at 1.5B tokens with a short test plan: 1) integration + small traffic 2) ramp to 20% production traffic 3) quality and latency checks (we’ll send prompts).

Procurement contact: procurement@fastpay.com — please copy them on the next email with the SOW and pricing, and include a line item that shows expected $/1M tokens at different tiers (pilot, mid, peak).

Thanks — looping in procurement when you have the SOW.

Best,
Anna Chen
Head of Product
FastPay
anna@fastpay.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: token profile, unit economics & next steps

Quick internal notes — copying pricing playbook excerpts for reference.

- Given their mid-range budget ($600k–$850k/mo) and 10–14M calls estimate: we should propose a tiered $/1M tokens table with committed tiers to protect both sides.
- Suggest: Pilot rate = $150 / 1M tokens (capped at 1.5B tokens) to cover ramp + support.
- Committed monthly band (12M calls -> ~7.2B tokens): propose $95 / 1M tokens for a 6–12 month commitment.
- If they commit to >15B tokens/month, we can drop to $75 / 1M tokens with additional SLA credits.

Context/architecture considerations (cc Dev):
- For the ~28% of calls needing >8k context, we can route to a 32k-quantized variant to reduce cost with minimal quality loss. For the 4–8% long cases, consider a separate batch job ingest (we can support 128k but price it as a higher-rate product).
- Call out caching prefix tokens and partial-history techniques — that often reduces prompt tokens by 10–30% for support flows.

Dev — can you validate we can support a 45-day pilot at the proposed caps with the routing rules above and an SLO of p95 latency < 400ms for single-turn completions?

—Lauren
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Chen <anna@fastpay.com>, procurement@fastpay.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token profile, unit economics & next steps

Anna / procurement team — thanks for confirming. Next steps from Redwood:

1) I’ll attach a 45-day pilot SOW and the pricing table (pilot rate + committed tiers) by EOD today. The SOW will reflect the 1.5B token cap and the three-stage ramp you requested.
2) Pricing table (summary):
   - Pilot (1.5B cap, 45 days): $150 / 1M tokens (estimated pilot invoice = $225k if fully used).
   - Committed (6–12 month): $95 / 1M tokens (applies at 7.2B / month band).
   - Enterprise (>15B / month): $75 / 1M tokens + SLA credits.
3) Engineering check: Dev (cc) — please confirm routing/32k variant availability and that we can enforce token caps + billing telemetry for the pilot.
4) Procurement: please confirm pilot PO process — we can accept a PO + a short MSA or proceed with DocuSign SOW if preferable.

If procurement wants an alternate price point within the $70–$120 / 1M tokens range Anna mentioned, we can run a committed volume model that hits the lower bound with longer commitment and consumption guarantees. Happy to discuss.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-estimate-v1.pdf, FastPay_token_sample_summary.csv

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
